items.headline: Trump Departs Beijing: Summit Closes Without Iran Off-Ramp; Post-Summit IRGC Cyber Window Opens; Tariff Truce Extended, 200 Boeing Jets Announced
items.summary: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit formal sessions concluded May 14-15, with Trump departing China today — closing the inhibiting window that had marginally suppressed IRGC retaliatory pre-positioning since May 12. CNN's May 15 reporting characterizes the summit as 'short on deliverables but with signs of a stabilized relationship,' with Trump and Xi 'making no specific announcements on trade, Taiwan, the war in Iran, or other points of contention' and 'coming away speaking of each other in warm terms.' Confirmed summit outputs: tariff truce extension (continuing the October 2025 Busan framework) and 200 Boeing commercial aircraft purchase announcements — China's first US commercial jet purchases in nearly a decade. No joint statement committing Xi to engage Tehran directly on Hormuz reopening or nuclear concessions was released. The summit's Iran track outcome is structurally identical to the pre-summit analyst consensus from CSIS, Chatham House, and CFR: symbolic stabilization output, not a binding pressure commitment on Tehran. With Trump now departing Beijing, the inhibiting effect on IRGC pre-positioning expires. The post-summit window — May 15 onward — is the highest-priority IRGC cyber watch period of the current crisis cycle. No Project Freedom resumption order has been confirmed as of this morning; any CENTCOM repositioning, White House War Powers congressional notification, or Trump Truth Social Iran signal in the next 24-72 hours is the highest-priority watch item of the post-summit period. Secondary market positive: the tariff truce extension removes a market uncertainty layer for the remainder of 2026, contributing alongside Cisco's AI supercycle earnings to modestly positive pre-market futures.

Fourth: the Trump administration delivered a formal message to Cuba signaling readiness to engage 'seriously on economic and security issues' pending Cuban fundamental changes; Havana signaled willingness to consider a $100M humanitarian aid offer.

items.headline: Warsh Era Day 1: April PPI +1.4% Monthly / Core +1.0% — 3.5x Consensus; Oil-Shock Inflation Accelerating; Rate-Cut vs. Hike Tension Immediate on Transition Day
items.summary: Kevin Warsh's Federal Reserve Chair era begins today — Powell's term expires May 15 — with the most adversely-inherited wholesale inflation data of any modern Fed Chair transition. April PPI data out this morning: +1.4% month-over-month versus the 0.4% consensus (3.5x expectations); core PPI +1.0% versus 0.3% consensus (3.3x expectations); annual PPI +6.0% versus 4.9% consensus. Shelter inflation doubled in April. The April PPI confirms aggressive upstream transmission of the Hormuz supply shock (Day 76) into US wholesale prices — the transmission is accelerating, not plateauing. Warsh was confirmed 54-45 on May 13 (Fetterman the lone Democratic crossover) under a dovish-leaning narrative; the PPI print immediately complicates that framing. Yahoo Finance and XTB analysis published this week flags the core tension: Warsh may need to hike, not cut, contradicting Trump's explicit and repeated public pressure for rate reductions. The inflation driver — Hormuz supply disruption — is immune to rate tools regardless of direction; rate cuts risk fueling price pressure, rate hikes risk compressing growth, and neither reopens the Strait. Warsh's inaugural public statement is expected today and will be parsed intensely for any rate-cut timeline signal, oil-shock inflation tolerance posture, and independence framing. His first FOMC meeting is June 16-17 — 32 days away. Powell remains on the Board of Governors through his governor term (January 2028).
